newsitem.title: RUSSIA: ING says some of its Russian MinFins unfrozen.
newsitem.headline: ING says some of its Russian MinFins unfrozen.

text.p: ING Bank Eurasia said Russian authorities had unfrozen some of its MinFin bonds with a nominal value of $51,000.

"We had about $71,000 nominal value of MinFin bonds frozen when the problem of stolen MinFins emerged for the first time," bond dealer Maxim Arkhipov said but added the problem of frozen bonds was far from resolved.
Banking sources said in late August Russian police were preparing an order to freeze up to a further $7 million nominal of MinFin bonds.
Earlier this year the authorities froze $24.22 million of the dollar-denominated bonds, which had gone missing.
"When the information appeared that further bonds could be frozen, we received a letter from Vneshtorgbank confirming that our paper with a nominal value of $51,000 on their accounts were unfrozen."

Rumours about the first freeze started circulating in June, hitting prices of the paper, which is traded both in Russia and abroad. Subsequently the finance ministry said it would not service the frozen bonds.
"We confirm to everybody it (the unfreezing of the bonds) has happened but there was no mention of other papers' fate," Arkhipov said.
"It does not look like the resolution of the whole problem because this amount is nothing," he added.
